editorial.headline: Advertising in Indonesia: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans campaign-making, media placement and brand work; it is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its permanent risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
Advertising in this classification is more than buying media space. It covers the creation and execution of advertising campaigns, advertising placement, brand-identity creation and brand development, campaign management, and the development of creative advertising materials. That work may appear in periodicals and newspapers, radio and television, on the internet and digital media, or through other media, for sports content as well as other fields. It also includes the design of display-location structures, connecting the creative message with the environment in which it is encountered.

The scope is deliberately broad in its practical expression. It encompasses advertising in print, broadcast, online and outdoor formats; media representation through the sale of advertising space and time; aerial advertising; distribution of advertising materials or samples; and the provision of billboard space and similar sites. It also reaches exhibition stands and other advertising locations, alongside marketing campaigns intended to attract and retain customers. Product promotion, point-of-sale marketing and direct mail sit within that same commercial terrain. Advertising agencies and media representatives are the providers generally associated with the activity.

The registration field is open across the full enterprise spectrum: micro, small, medium and large businesses. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In plain terms, a foreign investor may hold the entire business at the national level. The record grounds that position in Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021; it does not attach a lower foreign-equity ceiling or an additional national condition.

Bali produces a different result, and it should be read as a decisive local constraint rather than a minor qualification. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the large-business scale, every scope is assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The record identifies the moratorium as taking effect in May 2026. National openness therefore remains real, but it does not create a PMA registration path for this activity in Bali under the stated provincial rule.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, 100% foreign ownership is open; in Bali, the permanent PMA moratorium closes the registration path.
